analysis: Cross-source read: the tape is unchanged from the 5am brief — this is still a rates-driven session, not a company-news session. The 10Y held ~5.13-5.14% (fresh quote as high as 5.139-5.140%, highest since July 2007; 30Y at 5.438%, highest since 2004) and October-hike odds crept from ~71% (CME FedWatch) to >75% in one morning snapshot; futures stayed red with the Nasdaq the laggard (-1.0% to -1.2% across snapshots). New since the 5am brief: (1) JPMorgan raised its Meta target to $920 from $820 (Doug Anmuth), calling Muse potentially 'the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT' — real analyst action cutting against the Connect sell-the-news tape, though Morgan Stanley stayed at $775; (2) Reuters corroborated the chip selloff (NVDA -1%, MRVL/INTC -3% each), lifting that item from single-source to confirmed; (3) gold futures slipped ~1% to ~$4,290 and Bitcoin to ~$83,500. The Trump-Xi summit begins today with no new readouts — Bessent's truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 stands, and Reuters cautions major breakthroughs are not expected. Signal vs noise: the JPM target raise is confirmed multi-outlet analyst action; the CPO Cox insider-sale report, the AMZN $3B India commitment, and the Generac/AMZN deal date remain single-source and fragile. HN (Algolia, by-date and story searches) and Reddit sweeps found no qualifying threads.

headlines.headline: 10Y Treasury yield ~5.13-5.14%, near a 20-year high (closed Wednesday at the highest since July 2007); 30Y at 5.438%, highest since 2004; 2Y at 4.90%. Fed funds futures price a ~71% (CME FedWatch) to >75% chance of a 25bp October hike; NY Fed's John Williams said another hike this year is a 'reasonable' expectation.
headlines.why_it_matters: The entire curve repricing higher is the macro variable squeezing growth multiples — the October-hike odds are what is being watched into the open.

headlines.headline: Brent crude +1.5-1.7% at ~$104.80/bbl and WTI +1.3% at ~$93.35/bbl as the US-Iran conflict shows no sign of resolution.
headlines.why_it_matters: Higher energy costs feed inflation expectations, pulling forward rate-hike bets — a second leg of pressure on yields.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan raised its META target to $920 from $820 (Doug Anmuth), saying Muse could become 'the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT' and that retail connectors (Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair) could eventually monetize via a take-rate model. Morgan Stanley kept its $775 target.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh analyst support cuts against the sell-the-news tape — a $920 target well above the premarket price reframes the capex/spend debate into a monetization story.

headlines.headline: Meta fell ~2% premarket ($729.59 vs $744.10 close) the morning after Meta Connect, where it unveiled $1,299 VR glasses (100g), a pocket-sized 'Muse Charm' AI device, and retail connectors (Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair). CPO Christopher Cox disclosed selling 40,000 shares (~$28.5M) — single-source, unconfirmed beyond one outlet.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic sell-the-news after a ~30% monthly run-up; the CPO insider sale (single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile) can amplify the selloff narrative, and hardware/Muse spending re-raises capex questions.

headlines.headline: Chip stocks extending premarket losses: NVDA -1%, MRVL and INTC about -3% each (Reuters); AMD ~-2% (TipRanks). TD Cowen kept a Hold on Intel with a $115 price target.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rate-driven multiple compression hitting the AI trade broadly, independent of any new NVDA-specific catalyst — keeps the Stevens insider-sale overhang in a weak tape.

headlines.headline: Tesla added Grok AI to AMD-chip cars (software 2025.26+, via Wi-Fi or Premium Connectivity); August EU registrations came in at 15,430 (+4% YoY). Stock +0.45% premarket at $380.62; Elon Musk is invited to Trump's White House meeting with Xi today.
headlines.why_it_matters: A small AI-optionality lift against the FSD-probe and Q3 delivery-cut overhang; the Xi-meeting invite adds a trade-policy angle to the name today.

headlines.headline: Tim Cook is invited to Trump's meeting with China's Xi in Washington today; top executives from GM, Meta, Apple, Amazon, and Tesla are also expected to meet Trump and Xi. No fresh Apple-specific news otherwise.
headlines.why_it_matters: Direct read-through to iPhone supply chain and tariff risk — the overhang behind the iPhone-18 price-hike news — with the truce extension as modest relief.

headlines.headline: Generac reportedly +33% premarket on a $2.4B long-term Amazon data-center generator deal (deliveries 2027-28, up to $8B total, Amazon granted a warrant) — the report's date could not be confirmed, so treat as carry rather than fresh. No fresh Amazon-specific news; the $3B India commitment remains single-source and unconfirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Reads through to Amazon's AI-infra buildout scale — but single-source with an unconfirmed date, so treat the deal figures as fragile.

headlines.headline: Day 1 of the Trump-Xi White House summit: trade truce extended to Jan 10, 2027 (Bessent, after talks with Vice Premier He Lifeng); Xi arrived Wednesday evening, greeted by Trump at Andrews AFB. Agenda: AI governance, rare earths, tariffs, fentanyl, Taiwan arms sales. State dinner tonight with tech CEOs including Tim Cook, Jensen Huang, Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, Jeff Bezos, and Sam Altman. Reuters cautions major breakthroughs are not expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: The summit is today's swing factor — AI regulation, tariff terms, rare earths, and Taiwan headlines can move tech and trade-exposed names intraday.
